revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Choosing a Time-Capsule Box
revealWordProblem.text: Your class is choosing a box for the time capsule. The store sells three rectangular-prism boxes: a Small box that is 2 ft × 1 ft × 1 ft, a Medium box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, and a Large box that is 2 ft × 2 ft × 1.5 ft. Compute the volume of each box in cubic feet. Which box should the class buy if they need to fit at least 5 cubic feet of items? Explain how you decided.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Small: V = 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³. Medium: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³. Large: V = 2 × 2 × 1.5 = 6 ft³. The class should buy the Large box because only its volume, 6 ft³, is at least 5 ft³.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
questions.explanation: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
Check the units. Area is square units (²), volume is cubic units (³).
Not quite. V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = ___ cubic inches.
hints: Spot the three edges: l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in. Volume fills the whole box, so all three matter.
Use V = l × w × h and remember the answer needs cubic units (in³), not square units.
Multiply 4 × 3 = 12 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 5 inches.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
questions.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Identifica las tres aristas: l = 4 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 5 pulg. El volumen llena toda la caja, así que las tres importan.
Usa V = l × a × h y recuerda que la respuesta necesita unidades cúbicas (pulg³), no cuadradas.
Multiplica 4 × 3 = 12 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 5 pulgadas.

questions.stem: A box has a volume of 36 cm³. Its length is 6 cm and width is 3 cm. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: That number is the length given in the problem — divide volume by the full base area to find height.
That's the width from the problem, not the height — divide the volume by length × width instead.
Check your division — find the full base area (length × width) before dividing into the volume.
hints: You're given the volume (36 cm³) plus two edges (6 cm and 3 cm). The height is what's missing.
Work backward: divide the volume by the base area (length × width) to uncover the height.
Find the base area first: 6 × 3 = 18 cm². Then ask what number times 18 gives 36.
questions.stemEs: Una caja tiene un volumen de 36 cm³. Su longitud es 6 cm y su ancho es 3 cm. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el volumen (36 cm³) más dos aristas (6 cm y 3 cm). Lo que falta es la altura.
Trabaja al revés: divide el volumen entre el área de la base (largo × ancho) para descubrir la altura.
Halla primero el área de la base: 6 × 3 = 18 cm². Luego pregunta qué número por 18 da 36.

questions.stem: How is volume different from area?
choices: Volume measures 3D space (cubic units); area measures 2D surface (square units)
Volume uses square units; area uses cubic units
Volume only applies to cubes; area applies to all shapes
questions.explanation: Volume measures the space inside a 3D shape (cubic units like in³). Area measures a flat 2D surface (square units like in²).
choiceFeedback: The units are swapped here — think about which measurement fills 3D space and which covers a flat surface.
Volume isn't just for cubes — it applies to any 3D shape, like prisms and pyramids too.
These two measurements are different — one covers a flat surface, and one fills a 3D space.
hints: Think dimensions: area covers a flat 2D surface, while volume fills a 3D space.
Match each measurement to its unit: flat surfaces get square units (²), filled space gets cubic units (³).
Picture a rug (flat) versus a fish tank (filled). Decide which is area and which is volume, then check each choice.
questions.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferencia el volumen del área?
questions.explanationEs: El volumen mide el espacio dentro de una figura de tres dimensiones (unidades cúbicas como in³). El área mide una superficie plana de dos dimensiones (unidades cuadradas como in²).
choicesEs: El volumen mide el espacio en 3D (unidades cúbicas); el área mide una superficie en 2D (unidades cuadradas)
El volumen usa unidades cuadradas; el área usa unidades cúbicas
El volumen solo aplica a los cubos; el área aplica a todas las figuras
hintsEs: Piensa en dimensiones: el área cubre una superficie plana 2D, mientras que el volumen llena un espacio 3D.
Une cada medida con su unidad: las superficies planas llevan unidades cuadradas (²) y el espacio lleno lleva unidades cúbicas (³).
Imagina una alfombra (plana) frente a una pecera (llena). Decide cuál es área y cuál es volumen, y luego revisa cada opción.

reviewHighlights.rule: Volume of Rectangular Prisms with Fractional Edges
reviewHighlights.formula: V = l × w × h = B × h
steps: 1. Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying
2. Multiply numerators across, multiply denominators across: V = (l · w · h)
3. Simplify the fraction and label with cubic units
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Volume of Rectangular Prisms is rounding a fractional edge length to the nearest whole number before multiplying, instead of using the exact fraction or decimal. For a box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, a student might round 1.5 down to 1 and compute 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³, but the correct volume uses the exact edge length: 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³ — a full cubic foot larger. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I multiply using the exact fractional or decimal edge length, or did I round it off first?'

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.4) An L-shaped room is made of two rectangles: 10 ft × 6 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft. What is the total area?
level1.explanation: Area 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Area 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Double one side: area doubles.
Double both sides: area × 4.
hints: The L-shape is already split into two rectangles for you: 10 × 6 and 4 × 3.
Find each rectangle's area separately with A = l × w, then combine — joined shapes mean adding.
Compute 10 × 6 and 4 × 3, then add the two results. Label your answer in sq ft.
level1.stemEs: Una habitación en forma de L está formada por dos rectángulos: 10 ft × 6 ft y 4 ft × 3 ft. ¿Cuál es el área total?
level1.explanationEs: Área 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Área 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
hintsEs: La figura en L ya está dividida en dos rectángulos por ti: 10 × 6 y 4 × 3.
Halla el área de cada rectángulo por separado con A = l × a y luego combínalas: figuras unidas significan sumar.
Calcula 10 × 6 y 4 × 3, y luego suma los dos resultados. Etiqueta tu respuesta en pies².

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.4) A rectangular patio is 15 ft × 10 ft with a 5 ft × 4 ft rectangular flower bed cut out. What is the remaining area?
level1.explanation: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Cutout = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Remaining = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Test: same perimeter, different areas?
A thin rectangle and a square can differ.
Perimeter does not determine area.
hints: The flower bed is CUT OUT of the patio — that phrase tells you which operation to use.
Find the full patio area (15 × 10) and the cutout area (5 × 4), then remove the cutout.
Compute 15 × 10 and 5 × 4, then subtract the flower bed's area from the patio's area.
level1.stemEs: Un patio rectangular mide 15 ft × 10 ft y tiene recortado un jardín rectangular de 5 ft × 4 ft. ¿Cuál es el área restante?
level1.explanationEs: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Recorte = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Área restante = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
hintsEs: El jardín está RECORTADO del patio: esa frase te dice qué operación usar.
Halla el área total del patio (15 × 10) y el área del recorte (5 × 4), y luego quita el recorte.
Calcula 15 × 10 y 5 × 4, y luego resta el área del jardín del área del patio.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.5) What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
level1.explanation: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: Add 7 + 3 instead of multiplying? Volume uses multiplication of all three edges.
Square inches (in²) measure area, not volume. Volume is cubic (in³).
Multiply all three dimensions: 7 × 3 × 4, not 7 × 3 ÷ 2.
hints: Notice the three edge lengths: l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in. Volume asks how much space fills the whole box.
Use the volume formula V = l × w × h, and remember volume is measured in cubic units (in³).
Start with 7 × 3 = 21 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 4 inches.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
level1.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Fíjate en las tres aristas: l = 7 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 4 pulg. El volumen pregunta cuánto espacio llena toda la caja.
Usa la fórmula del volumen V = l × a × h, y recuerda que el volumen se mide en unidades cúbicas (pulg³).
Empieza con 7 × 3 = 21 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 4 pulgadas.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.5) A time capsule box has a volume of 120 cm³. Its length is 10 cm and width is 4 cm. What is its height?
choiceFeedback: Check your division. 120 ÷ (10 × 4) = 120 ÷ 40 = ?
Did you use the formula h = V ÷ (l × w) correctly?
Verify: 10 × 4 × ? = 120. What number works?
hints: You already know the volume (120 cm³) and two edges (10 cm and 4 cm). The height is the missing piece.
Work backward: since V = l × w × h, divide the volume by the base area (length × width) to find the height.
First find the base area: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Then figure out what number times 40 gives 120.
level1.stemEs: Una caja de cápsula del tiempo tiene un volumen de 120 cm³. Su largo es 10 cm y su ancho es 4 cm. ¿Cuál es su altura?
hintsEs: Ya conoces el volumen (120 cm³) y dos aristas (10 cm y 4 cm). La altura es la pieza que falta.
Trabaja al revés: como V = l × a × h, divide el volumen entre el área de la base (largo × ancho) para hallar la altura.
Primero halla el área de la base: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Luego averigua qué número por 40 da 120.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.6) A rectangular prism has l = 6 in, w = 4 in, h = 2 in. What is its surface area?
choiceFeedback: That's the volume — surface area needs the sum of all six face areas, not length × width × height.
Check the units — surface area covers a flat surface, so it needs square units, not cubic.
Remember each face has a matching opposite face — double the sum of the three face areas.
hints: Surface area covers all 6 faces of the 6 × 4 × 2 box — it's not the same as the space inside.
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: find the three different face areas, double each, and add.
Start with the top face: 6 × 4 = 24 in². Then find 6 × 2 and 4 × 2 before doubling and adding.
level1.stemEs: Un prisma rectangular tiene l = 6 in, w = 4 in, h = 2 in. ¿Cuál es el área de su superficie?
hintsEs: El área superficial cubre las 6 caras de la caja de 6 × 4 × 2: no es lo mismo que el espacio de adentro.
Usa AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah: halla las tres áreas de cara distintas, duplica cada una y suma.
Empieza con la cara de arriba: 6 × 4 = 24 pulg². Luego halla 6 × 2 y 4 × 2 antes de duplicar y sumar.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.6) How many faces does a rectangular prism have?
level1.explanation: A rectangular prism has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, and right.
choiceFeedback: Don't forget the top and bottom — a box has faces all around it, not just the sides.
That's the number of corners (vertices), not the number of flat faces.
That's the number of edges, not the number of flat faces — count the flat surfaces instead.
hints: Picture a cereal box in your hands. Turn it: there's a front, a back, two sides, a top, and a bottom.
Count faces in opposite pairs — every face on a rectangular prism has a matching partner across from it.
Count the pairs: top/bottom is one pair, front/back is another, left/right is the third. Multiply pairs by 2.
level1.explanationEs: Un prisma rectangular tiene 6 caras: arriba, abajo, adelante, atrás, izquierda y derecha.
hintsEs: Imagina una caja de cereal en tus manos. Gírala: hay un frente, una parte trasera, dos lados, una tapa y una base.
Cuenta las caras en pares opuestos — cada cara de un prisma rectangular tiene una pareja igual del otro lado.
Cuenta los pares: arriba/abajo es un par, frente/atrás es otro, izquierda/derecha es el tercero. Multiplica los pares por 2.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.7) What is the surface area of a rectangular prism with l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
choiceFeedback: That's the volume — surface area adds up all six face areas instead of multiplying three edges.
Check the units — a surface measurement needs square units, not cubic.
You found half the faces — remember each face has a matching opposite face to double.
hints: You need surface area — the total of all 6 face areas of the 5 × 4 × 3 prism — not the space inside.
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: three different faces, each with a matching twin on the opposite side.
Find the three face areas first: 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15, and 4×3 = 12. Double each, then add the results.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de superficie de un prisma rectangular con l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
hintsEs: Necesitas el área superficial: el total de las 6 áreas de cara del prisma de 5 × 4 × 3, no el espacio de adentro.
Usa AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah: tres caras distintas, cada una con su gemela en el lado opuesto.
Halla primero las tres áreas de cara: 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15 y 4×3 = 12. Duplica cada una y luego suma los resultados.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.7) How many faces does a triangular prism have?
level1.explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular lateral faces.
choiceFeedback: Count again — a triangular prism has more rectangular sides than that, plus its two ends.
That's the face count for a rectangular prism — a triangular prism has one fewer face.
That's just the rectangular sides — don't forget the two triangular ends.
hints: Picture a tent or a triangular chocolate box: two triangle ends plus rectangles wrapping around the sides.
Count the two triangular bases first, then count one rectangle for each side of the triangle.
A triangle has 3 sides, so count 3 rectangular faces. Then add the triangular ends to that count.
level1.explanationEs: Un prisma triangular tiene 5 caras: 2 bases triangulares y 3 caras laterales rectangulares.
hintsEs: Imagina una tienda de campaña o una caja triangular de chocolates: dos extremos triangulares más rectángulos que envuelven los lados.
Cuenta primero las dos bases triangulares y luego cuenta un rectángulo por cada lado del triángulo.
Un triángulo tiene 3 lados, así que cuenta 3 caras rectangulares. Luego suma los extremos triangulares a ese conteo.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.8) A square pyramid has a base edge of 5 in and a slant height of 7 in. What is the surface area?
level1.explanation: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². SA = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
choiceFeedback: You calculated the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base area.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
Recheck each triangular face area — make sure you take half of base times slant height for each.
hints: A square pyramid has TWO kinds of faces: one square base (5 × 5) and four identical triangles with slant height 7.
SA = base area + 4 triangle areas, where each triangle is ½ × base edge × slant height.
Base first: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Then one triangle: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiply that by 4 and add the base area.
level1.stemEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene una arista de base de 5 in y una altura inclinada de 7 in. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
level1.explanationEs: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Cada cara lateral: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Cuatro caras: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². Área de superficie = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
hintsEs: Una pirámide cuadrangular tiene DOS tipos de caras: una base cuadrada (5 × 5) y cuatro triángulos idénticos con apotema de 7.
AS = área de la base + 4 áreas de triángulo, donde cada triángulo es ½ × arista de la base × apotema.
La base primero: 5 × 5 = 25 pulg². Luego un triángulo: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiplica eso por 4 y súmale el área de la base.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.8) How many lateral (triangular) faces does a square pyramid have?
level1.explanation: A square pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular lateral faces — one for each side of the square.
choiceFeedback: A square base has four sides — count a triangular face for each side of the square.
The square base isn't a lateral (triangular) face — only count the slanted triangle sides.
That's too many — count only the slanted triangular sides around the square base.
hints: Lateral faces are the slanted triangles on the sides — the square base itself doesn't count.
Each side of the square base holds up exactly one triangle. Count the sides of a square.
Trace the base: it's a square. Count one triangle leaning against each side of that square.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuántas caras laterales (triangulares) tiene una pirámide cuadrada?
level1.explanationEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene una base cuadrada y 4 caras laterales triangulares, una por cada lado del cuadrado.
hintsEs: Las caras laterales son los triángulos inclinados de los lados; la base cuadrada no cuenta.
Cada lado de la base cuadrada sostiene exactamente un triángulo. Cuenta los lados de un cuadrado.
Traza la base: es un cuadrado. Cuenta un triángulo apoyado en cada lado de ese cuadrado.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.9) A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle?
level1.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 31.2 is 6 × 5.2 — the full rectangle. One triangle is half of that: multiply by ½.
11.2 comes from adding 6 + 5.2. Area means multiply base × height, then take half.
The number is right, but ft measures length. Area needs square units (sq ft).
hints: Focus on just ONE of the 6 triangles: its base is 6 ft and its height is 5.2 ft.
One triangle uses A = ½ × b × h — don't multiply by 6 yet; that step is for the whole hexagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5.2: take half of 6 first, then multiply by 5.2. Label it in sq ft.
level1.stemEs: Un hexágono regular se divide en 6 triángulos iguales desde el centro. Cada triángulo tiene una base de 6 ft y una altura de 5.2 ft. ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo?
level1.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Concéntrate en solo UNO de los 6 triángulos: su base es de 6 pies y su altura de 5.2 pies.
Un triángulo usa A = ½ × b × h; todavía no multipliques por 6, ese paso es para el hexágono completo.
Calcula ½ × 6 × 5.2: saca primero la mitad de 6 y luego multiplica por 5.2. Etiquétalo en pies².

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.9) Using the triangle from the previous question, what is the total area of the hexagonal skylight?
level1.explanation: Total area = 6 triangles × 15.6 sq ft = 93.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: That is the area of ONE of the congruent triangles. The hexagon is made of 6 of them — how many triangle areas do you still need to add?
You multiplied by 12 instead of 6. Count the congruent triangles the hexagon decomposes into before you multiply.
That is 4 triangles, not 6. Re-count how many congruent triangles the hexagon breaks into.
hints: You already found one triangle's area (15.6 sq ft) in the last question — now think about the whole hexagon.
A regular hexagon splits into 6 identical triangles, so the total is 6 copies of one triangle's area.
Multiply 15.6 × 6. (Tip: do 15 × 6, then 0.6 × 6, and combine.)
level1.stemEs: Usando el triángulo de la pregunta anterior, ¿cuál es el área total del tragaluz hexagonal?
level1.explanationEs: Área total = 6 triángulos × 15.6 pies cuadrados = 93.6 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Ya hallaste el área de un triángulo (15.6 pies²) en la pregunta anterior; ahora piensa en el hexágono completo.
Un hexágono regular se divide en 6 triángulos idénticos, así que el total son 6 copias del área de un triángulo.
Multiplica 15.6 × 6. (Consejo: haz 15 × 6, luego 0.6 × 6 y combina.)

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.10) What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
level1.explanation: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
Check the units. Area is square units (²), volume is cubic units (³).
Not quite. V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = ___ cubic inches.
hints: Spot the three edges: l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in. Volume fills the whole box, so all three matter.
Use V = l × w × h and remember the answer needs cubic units (in³), not square units.
Multiply 4 × 3 = 12 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 5 inches.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
level1.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Identifica las tres aristas: l = 4 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 5 pulg. El volumen llena toda la caja, así que las tres importan.
Usa V = l × a × h y recuerda que la respuesta necesita unidades cúbicas (pulg³), no cuadradas.
Multiplica 4 × 3 = 12 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 5 pulgadas.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.10) A box has a volume of 36 cm³. Its length is 6 cm and width is 3 cm. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: That number is the length given in the problem — divide volume by the full base area to find height.
That's the width from the problem, not the height — divide the volume by length × width instead.
Check your division — find the full base area (length × width) before dividing into the volume.
hints: You're given the volume (36 cm³) plus two edges (6 cm and 3 cm). The height is what's missing.
Work backward: divide the volume by the base area (length × width) to uncover the height.
Find the base area first: 6 × 3 = 18 cm². Then ask what number times 18 gives 36.
level1.stemEs: Una caja tiene un volumen de 36 cm³. Su longitud es 6 cm y su ancho es 3 cm. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el volumen (36 cm³) más dos aristas (6 cm y 3 cm). Lo que falta es la altura.
Trabaja al revés: divide el volumen entre el área de la base (largo × ancho) para descubrir la altura.
Halla primero el área de la base: 6 × 3 = 18 cm². Luego pregunta qué número por 18 da 36.

level2.stem: Two boxes: Box A is 10 × 5 × 4 inches. Box B is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Which has more volume and by how much?
level2.explanation: Box A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Box B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Box B is bigger by 40 in³.
choiceFeedback: Recheck which box's volume is larger — recalculate both totals before comparing.
You picked the right box, but recheck the subtraction to find the exact difference.
These two volumes aren't equal — calculate each box's volume and compare the totals.
hints: This asks two things: which box holds more AND by how many cubic inches — so find both volumes first.
Compute each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger.
Box A: 10 × 5 = 50, then × 4. Box B: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Compare the two totals.
level2.stemEs: Dos cajas: la caja A mide 10 × 5 × 4 pulgadas. La caja B mide 8 × 6 × 5 pulgadas. ¿Cuál tiene más volumen y por cuánto?
level2.explanationEs: Caja A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Caja B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. La caja B es mayor por 40 in³.
hintsEs: Esto pregunta dos cosas: cuál caja guarda más Y por cuántas pulgadas cúbicas, así que halla primero ambos volúmenes.
Calcula cada volumen con V = l × a × h y luego resta el total menor del mayor.
Caja A: 10 × 5 = 50 y luego × 4. Caja B: 8 × 6 = 48 y luego × 5. Compara los dos totales.

level2.stem: What is the volume of a prism with edge lengths 1/2 m, 3 m, and 4 m?
choiceFeedback: Adding the three edge lengths together won't give volume — multiply them instead.
Check the fractional edge — make sure you multiply by 1/2, not treat it as a whole number.
That's just one edge length — volume needs all three dimensions multiplied together.
hints: One edge is a fraction: 1/2 m. The other edges are 3 m and 4 m. The formula works the same with fractions.
Multiply all three edges: V = 1/2 × 3 × 4. Multiplying by 1/2 is the same as dividing by 2.
Multiply the whole numbers first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then take half of that result.
level2.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma con longitudes de arista de 1/2 m, 3 m y 4 m?
hintsEs: Una arista es una fracción: 1/2 m. Las otras aristas son 3 m y 4 m. La fórmula funciona igual con fracciones.
Multiplica las tres aristas: V = 1/2 × 3 × 4. Multiplicar por 1/2 es lo mismo que dividir entre 2.
Multiplica primero los números enteros: 3 × 4 = 12. Luego saca la mitad de ese resultado.

level2.stem: A cube has an edge length of 5 cm. What is its volume?
level2.explanation: A cube's volume is edge³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.
choiceFeedback: Adding the edge three times won't give volume — multiply the edge by itself three times instead.
You squared the edge but forgot to multiply by it once more — a cube's volume needs edge × edge × edge.
Check your last multiplication — multiply the squared edge by the same edge length again.
hints: A cube's edges are all equal, so its length, width, and height are each 5 cm.
Use V = edge × edge × edge — multiply 5 by itself three times, not 5 × 3.
Start with 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply that result by 5 one more time.
level2.stemEs: Un cubo tiene una longitud de arista de 5 cm. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
level2.explanationEs: El volumen de un cubo es arista³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.
hintsEs: Las aristas de un cubo son todas iguales, así que su largo, ancho y altura son 5 cm cada uno.
Usa V = arista × arista × arista: multiplica 5 por sí mismo tres veces, no 5 × 3.
Empieza con 5 × 5 = 25 y luego multiplica ese resultado por 5 una vez más.

level2.stem: A time-capsule box measures 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall. What is its volume?
level2.explanation: V = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic in. Volume uses cubic units.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
You multiplied two dimensions but forgot the third — include length, width, AND height.
Check the units — this fills 3D space, so it needs cubic units, not square units.
level2.stemEs: Una caja para una cápsula del tiempo mide 6 in de largo, 4 in de ancho y 3 in de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
level2.explanationEs: V = largo × ancho × alto = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 pulgadas cúbicas. El volumen usa unidades cúbicas.
hints: Volume measures the space inside a solid, and it is always labeled in cubic units.
Use V = length × width × height: multiply two of the dimensions first, then multiply by the third.
Start with 6 × 4 = 24. Now multiply that result by the height of 3.
hintsEs: El volumen mide el espacio dentro de un cuerpo y siempre se escribe en unidades cúbicas.
Usa V = largo × ancho × alto: multiplica primero dos de las dimensiones y luego multiplica por la tercera.
Empieza con 6 × 4 = 24. Ahora multiplica ese resultado por la altura de 3.

level2.stem: Two storage boxes are ready to pack. Box A is 5 × 5 × 2 inches and Box B is 4 × 4 × 3 inches. Which box holds more?
choices: Box A, because 50 cubic in is more than 48 cubic in
Box B, because 48 cubic in is more than 50 cubic in
Box B, because it is taller
level2.explanation: Box A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 cubic in. Box B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cubic in. 50 > 48, so Box A holds more.
choiceFeedback: Compare the two volume numbers again — which one is actually larger?
The two boxes have different volumes — calculate each one and compare the totals.
Height alone doesn't decide which holds more — compare the full volumes instead.
level2.stemEs: Hay dos cajas de almacenamiento listas para empacar. La caja A mide 5 × 5 × 2 pulgadas y la caja B mide 4 × 4 × 3 pulgadas. ¿Cuál caja guarda más?
level2.explanationEs: Caja A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 pulgadas cúbicas. Caja B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 pulgadas cúbicas. 50 > 48, así que la caja A guarda más.
hints: How much a box holds is its volume, not its height or its widest side.
Find the volume of each box separately with V = l × w × h, then compare the two numbers.
For Box A, 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply by 2. Do the same kind of work for Box B before comparing.
hintsEs: Lo que cabe en una caja es su volumen, no su altura ni su lado más ancho.
Halla el volumen de cada caja por separado con V = l × w × h y luego compara los dos números.
Para la caja A, 5 × 5 = 25 y luego multiplica por 2. Haz el mismo trabajo con la caja B antes de comparar.
choicesEs: La caja A, porque 50 pulgadas cúbicas es más que 48 pulgadas cúbicas
La caja B, porque 48 pulgadas cúbicas es más que 50 pulgadas cúbicas
La caja B, porque es más alta

level2.stem: A keepsake box is 4 in long, 3 in wide, and 1½ in tall. What is its volume?
level2.explanation: V = 4 × 3 × 1.5 = 12 × 1.5 = 18 cubic in. A fractional edge does not change the steps.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
You found the base area but forgot to multiply by the height for volume.
Double check the height value — using the wrong height changes your answer too much.
level2.stemEs: Una caja de recuerdos mide 4 in de largo, 3 in de ancho y 1½ in de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
level2.explanationEs: V = 4 × 3 × 1.5 = 12 × 1.5 = 18 pulgadas cúbicas. Una arista fraccionaria no cambia los pasos.
hints: A fractional edge length works exactly like a whole-number one — the formula V = l × w × h does not change.
Multiply the two whole-number edges first, then multiply that product by the fractional height.
4 × 3 = 12. Now multiply 12 by 1½, which you can split into 12 × 1 plus 12 × ½.
hintsEs: Una arista fraccionaria funciona igual que una entera: la fórmula V = l × w × h no cambia.
Multiplica primero las dos aristas enteras y después multiplica ese producto por la altura fraccionaria.
4 × 3 = 12. Ahora multiplica 12 por 1½, que puedes separar en 12 × 1 más 12 × ½.

level2.stem: (Lesson 5.5) Two storage bins: Bin A is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Bin B is 9 × 4 × 7 inches. Which holds more and by how much?
level2.explanation: Bin A: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Bin B: 9 × 4 × 7 = 252 in³. Bin B holds 12 in³ more.
choiceFeedback: Calculate both volumes first: Bin A = 8 × 6 × 5 and Bin B = 9 × 4 × 7.
Which bin has the larger volume? Find the difference.
Check your arithmetic: 8 × 6 × 5 = ? and 9 × 4 × 7 = ?
hints: This is a two-part question: which bin holds more AND by how many cubic inches. You need both volumes first.
Find each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger to get the difference.
Start with Bin A: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Next do Bin B: 9 × 4 = 36, then × 7. Compare the totals.
level2.stemEs: Dos cajas de almacenamiento: la Caja A mide 8 × 6 × 5 pulgadas. La Caja B mide 9 × 4 × 7 pulgadas. ¿Cuál guarda más y por cuánto?
level2.explanationEs: Caja A: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Caja B: 9 × 4 × 7 = 252 in³. La Caja B guarda 12 in³ más.
hintsEs: Esta pregunta tiene dos partes: cuál caja guarda más Y por cuántas pulgadas cúbicas. Necesitas ambos volúmenes primero.
Halla cada volumen con V = l × a × h y luego resta el total menor del mayor para obtener la diferencia.
Empieza con la Caja A: 8 × 6 = 48 y luego × 5. Después la Caja B: 9 × 4 = 36 y luego × 7. Compara los totales.

level2.stem: (Lesson 5.6) A cube has edges of 5 cm. What is its surface area?
level2.explanation: A cube has 6 identical faces. Each face: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Total SA = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².
choiceFeedback: That's the volume calculation (edge cubed) — surface area needs six face areas added together.
Check the units — a flat surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
Square the edge length for one face's area first, then multiply by the number of faces.
hints: A cube's 6 faces are identical squares, each one 5 cm by 5 cm.
Find the area of one square face, then multiply by 6 — and keep square units (cm²).
One face is 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Now multiply that area by the number of faces, 6.
level2.stemEs: Un cubo tiene aristas de 5 cm. ¿Cuál es el área de su superficie?
level2.explanationEs: Un cubo tiene 6 caras idénticas. Cada cara: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Área total de la superficie = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².
hintsEs: Las 6 caras de un cubo son cuadrados idénticos, cada uno de 5 cm por 5 cm.
Halla el área de una cara cuadrada y luego multiplica por 6, conservando las unidades cuadradas (cm²).
Una cara es 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Ahora multiplica esa área por el número de caras, 6.

level2.stem: (Lesson 5.7) A triangular prism has triangular bases with base 6 in and height 4 in. The prism is 10 in long and the two slant sides of the triangle are each 5 in. What is the surface area?
level2.explanation: Triangular bases: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Three rectangular faces: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². SA = 24 + 160 = 184 in².
choiceFeedback: You added the three rectangular faces but left out the two triangular bases.
You added the two slanted rectangular faces and the bases but missed the bottom rectangular face.
Check the units — a wrapped surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Gather the parts: two triangle bases (base 6 in, height 4 in) and three rectangles, each 10 in long.
SA = 2 triangle areas + 3 rectangle areas. Each rectangle is one triangle side (6, 5, or 5) times the 10 in length.
Triangles first: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, doubled is 24 in². Then find the rectangles: 6 × 10, 5 × 10, and 5 × 10.
level2.stemEs: Un prisma triangular tiene bases triangulares con base 6 in y altura 4 in. El prisma mide 10 in de largo y los dos lados inclinados del triángulo miden 5 in cada uno. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
level2.explanationEs: Bases triangulares: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Tres caras rectangulares: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². Área de superficie = 24 + 160 = 184 in².
hintsEs: Reúne las partes: dos bases triangulares (base 6 pulg, altura 4 pulg) y tres rectángulos, cada uno de 10 pulg de largo.
AS = 2 áreas de triángulo + 3 áreas de rectángulo. Cada rectángulo es un lado del triángulo (6, 5 o 5) por el largo de 10 pulg.
Los triángulos primero: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, duplicado son 24 pulg². Luego halla los rectángulos: 6 × 10, 5 × 10 y 5 × 10.

level2.stem: (Lesson 5.8) A square pyramid has a base area of 49 cm² and a total lateral area of 84 cm². What is the surface area?
level2.explanation: SA = Base Area + Lateral Area = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
choiceFeedback: That's just the lateral area — add the base area too for total surface area.
That's just the base area — add the lateral (triangular) area too for the total.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Both pieces are already given: base area 49 cm² and lateral (triangle) area 84 cm².
Total surface area = base area + lateral area — one addition, keeping square units.
Set up the sum 49 + 84 and add carefully, keeping cm² in your answer.
level2.stemEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene un área de base de 49 cm² y un área lateral total de 84 cm². ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
level2.explanationEs: Área de superficie = área de la base + área lateral = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
hintsEs: Ya te dan las dos piezas: área de la base 49 cm² y área lateral (de los triángulos) 84 cm².
Área superficial total = área de la base + área lateral: una sola suma, conservando las unidades cuadradas.
Plantea la suma 49 + 84 y súmala con cuidado, conservando cm² en tu respuesta.

level2.stem: (Lesson 5.10) Two boxes: Box A is 10 × 5 × 4 inches. Box B is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Which has more volume and by how much?
level2.explanation: Box A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Box B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Box B is bigger by 40 in³.
choiceFeedback: Recheck which box's volume is larger — recalculate both totals before comparing.
You picked the right box, but recheck the subtraction to find the exact difference.
These two volumes aren't equal — calculate each box's volume and compare the totals.
hints: This asks two things: which box holds more AND by how many cubic inches — so find both volumes first.
Compute each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger.
Box A: 10 × 5 = 50, then × 4. Box B: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Compare the two totals.
level2.stemEs: Dos cajas: la caja A mide 10 × 5 × 4 pulgadas. La caja B mide 8 × 6 × 5 pulgadas. ¿Cuál tiene más volumen y por cuánto?
level2.explanationEs: Caja A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Caja B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. La caja B es mayor por 40 in³.
hintsEs: Esto pregunta dos cosas: cuál caja guarda más Y por cuántas pulgadas cúbicas, así que halla primero ambos volúmenes.
Calcula cada volumen con V = l × a × h y luego resta el total menor del mayor.
Caja A: 10 × 5 = 50 y luego × 4. Caja B: 8 × 6 = 48 y luego × 5. Compara los dos totales.

level3.prompt: A toy company ships action figures in boxes that are 4 × 3 × 6 inches. A shipping crate is 24 × 12 × 18 inches. How many action figure boxes fit in the crate? Explain your reasoning step by step.
level3.sentenceFrame: Each toy box has a volume of ___ in³. The crate has a volume of ___ in³. I can fit ___ boxes because ___. I checked by ___.
level3.hint: Find three different factor combinations of the target volume.
hints: Two sizes matter: each toy box is 4 × 3 × 6 in and the crate is 24 × 12 × 18 in. Each crate edge is a multiple of a box edge.
Find both volumes, then divide the crate's volume by one box's volume. Check by counting rows, columns, and layers.
Start with one toy box: multiply 4 × 3 = 12, then multiply by 6. Next find the crate's volume the same way.
level3.explanation: Each toy box holds 4 × 3 × 6 = 72 in³ and the crate holds 24 × 12 × 18 = 5184 in³, so 5184 ÷ 72 = 72 boxes fit. The division comes out exact because every crate edge is a whole-number multiple of a box edge: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 across, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 deep, and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 layers, and 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 confirms it.
level3.explanationEs: Cada caja de juguete tiene 4 × 3 × 6 = 72 in³ y la caja grande tiene 24 × 12 × 18 = 5184 in³, así que caben 5184 ÷ 72 = 72 cajas. La división sale exacta porque cada lado de la caja grande es un múltiplo entero de un lado de la caja pequeña: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 a lo ancho, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 de fondo y 18 ÷ 6 = 3 capas, y 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 lo confirma.
level3.promptEs: Una juguetería envía figuras de acción en cajas de 4 × 3 × 6 pulgadas. Una caja de embarque mide 24 × 12 × 18 pulgadas. ¿Cuántas cajas de figuras caben en la caja de embarque? Explica tu razonamiento paso a paso.
hintsEs: Importan dos tamaños: cada caja de juguetes mide 4 × 3 × 6 pulg y el cajón mide 24 × 12 × 18 pulg. Cada arista del cajón es múltiplo de una arista de la caja.
Halla ambos volúmenes y luego divide el volumen del cajón entre el de una caja. Compruébalo contando filas, columnas y capas.
Empieza con una caja de juguetes: multiplica 4 × 3 = 12 y luego multiplica por 6. Después halla el volumen del cajón igual.

level3.stem: A fish tank measures 2 1/2 ft by 2 ft by 3 ft. What is its volume?
choiceFeedback: You multiplied two dimensions but left out the third edge length.
Check the fractional edge length — rounding it down changes your answer.
Double check your multiplication — recompute each step to avoid doubling the result.
hints: One dimension is a mixed number: 2 1/2 ft. Rewrite it as 2.5 before multiplying.
Use V = l × w × h with all three numbers: 2.5 × 2 × 3. Keep the half — don't round it away.
Multiply the easy pair first: 2 × 3 = 6. Then multiply that result by 2.5.
level3.stemEs: Una pecera mide 2 1/2 ft por 2 ft por 3 ft. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
hintsEs: Una dimensión es un número mixto: 2 1/2 pies. Reescríbela como 2.5 antes de multiplicar.
Usa V = largo × ancho × alto con los tres números: 2.5 × 2 × 3. Conserva la mitad — no la redondees.
Multiplica primero el par fácil: 2 × 3 = 6. Luego multiplica ese resultado por 2.5.

level3.stem: A prism with a 3/4 ft by 2 ft base has a volume of 9 ft³. What is its height?
choiceFeedback: Recalculate the base area first (3/4 × 2), then divide the volume by that.
That's the volume given, not the height — divide it by the base area to find height.
Make sure you find the full base area — multiply both base dimensions before dividing.
hints: You know the volume (9 ft³) and the base dimensions (3/4 ft and 2 ft). The height is missing.
Height = Volume ÷ base area. Find the base area first, then divide the volume by it.
Base area: 3/4 × 2 = 1.5 ft². Now ask what number times 1.5 equals 9.
level3.stemEs: Un prisma con una base de 3/4 ft por 2 ft tiene un volumen de 9 ft³. ¿Cuál es su altura?
level3.explanationEs: Altura = V ÷ (área de la base) = 9 ÷ (3/4 × 2) = 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6 ft.
hintsEs: Conoces el volumen (9 pies³) y las dimensiones de la base (3/4 pie y 2 pies). Falta la altura.
Altura = Volumen ÷ área de la base. Halla primero el área de la base y luego divide el volumen entre ella.
Área de la base: 3/4 × 2 = 1.5 pies². Ahora pregunta qué número por 1.5 da 9.

level3.stem: A time-capsule box measures 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall. What is its volume?
level3.explanation: V = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic in. Volume uses cubic units.

You multiplied two dimensions but forgot the third — include length, width, AND height.
Check the units — this fills 3D space, so it needs cubic units, not square units.

level3.explanationEs: V = largo × ancho × alto = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 pulgadas cúbicas. El volumen usa unidades cúbicas.
hints: Volume measures the space inside a solid, and it is always labeled in cubic units.
Use V = length × width × height: multiply two of the dimensions first, then multiply by the third.
Start with 6 × 4 = 24. Now multiply that result by the height of 3.
hintsEs: El volumen mide el espacio dentro de un cuerpo y siempre se escribe en unidades cúbicas.
Usa V = largo × ancho × alto: multiplica primero dos de las dimensiones y luego multiplica por la tercera.
Empieza con 6 × 4 = 24. Ahora multiplica ese resultado por la altura de 3.

level3.stem: Two storage boxes are ready to pack. Box A is 5 × 5 × 2 inches and Box B is 4 × 4 × 3 inches. Which box holds more?
choices: Box A, because 50 cubic in is more than 48 cubic in
Box B, because 48 cubic in is more than 50 cubic in
Box B, because it is taller
level3.explanation: Box A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 cubic in. Box B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cubic in. 50 > 48, so Box A holds more.
choiceFeedback: Compare the two volume numbers again — which one is actually larger?
The two boxes have different volumes — calculate each one and compare the totals.
Height alone doesn't decide which holds more — compare the full volumes instead.
level3.stemEs: Hay dos cajas de almacenamiento listas para empacar. La caja A mide 5 × 5 × 2 pulgadas y la caja B mide 4 × 4 × 3 pulgadas. ¿Cuál caja guarda más?
level3.explanationEs: Caja A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 pulgadas cúbicas. Caja B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 pulgadas cúbicas. 50 > 48, así que la caja A guarda más.
hints: How much a box holds is its volume, not its height or its widest side.
Find the volume of each box separately with V = l × w × h, then compare the two numbers.
For Box A, 5 × 5 = 25, then multiply by 2. Do the same kind of work for Box B before comparing.
hintsEs: Lo que cabe en una caja es su volumen, no su altura ni su lado más ancho.
Halla el volumen de cada caja por separado con V = l × w × h y luego compara los dos números.
Para la caja A, 5 × 5 = 25 y luego multiplica por 2. Haz el mismo trabajo con la caja B antes de comparar.
choicesEs: La caja A, porque 50 pulgadas cúbicas es más que 48 pulgadas cúbicas
La caja B, porque 48 pulgadas cúbicas es más que 50 pulgadas cúbicas
La caja B, porque es más alta

level3.stem: A box has a volume of 24 cm³. Give THREE different sets of whole-number edge lengths that work. Then explain why doubling just ONE edge doubles the volume, but doubling ALL THREE multiplies it by 8 — not by 6.
level3.stemEs: Una caja tiene un volumen de 24 cm³. Da TRES conjuntos distintos de aristas con números enteros que funcionen. Después explica por qué duplicar UNA sola arista duplica el volumen, pero duplicar LAS TRES lo multiplica por 8 — no por 6.
level3.modelAnswer: Three that work: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24, 1 × 4 × 6 = 24, and 2 × 2 × 6 = 24. Volume multiplies the three edges, so doubling one edge multiplies the product by 2: 2 × 3 × 8 = 48. Doubling all three multiplies by 2 three times — 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 — so 24 becomes 192. It is not 6 because the edges are multiplied together, not added; 2 + 2 + 2 would be the answer if volume were a sum, and it is not.
level3.modelAnswerEs: Tres que funcionan: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24, 1 × 4 × 6 = 24 y 2 × 2 × 6 = 24. El volumen multiplica las tres aristas, así que duplicar una arista multiplica el producto por 2: 2 × 3 × 8 = 48. Duplicar las tres multiplica por 2 tres veces — 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 — así que 24 se convierte en 192. No es 6 porque las aristas se multiplican, no se suman; 2 + 2 + 2 sería la respuesta si el volumen fuera una suma, y no lo es.
